title: Pilot sequence
summary: Expand through concrete reviewable deliverables and measured acceptance.

sections.label: Possible stages for an automation pilot
rows: One process, reviewed examples and current effort
Results and evidence for a limited task
Limited changes under the agreed checks and authority
Whether quality and operating effort are acceptable
Whether an added decision component helps
Defined operating ownership, limits and recovery

sections.label: First deliverable
sections.text: Record a representative task, its expected result and the evidence needed to judge it. Set acceptance criteria with the relevant owners before collecting results. Select only the stages the trial needs.

sections.label: Optional Jev example
sections.text: For a country-data curation study, a Jev shadow comparison can test source-support judgments. It is not a required stage for other workflows or proof of the separate Atlas suggestion pilot.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Expand only where quality and accepted-result economics improve. Select durable infrastructure from demonstrated execution requirements.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Use the existing experiment-plan mapping to define a bounded trial and a reviewable expansion decision.
Record the current process, trial scope and agreed acceptance before collecting outcomes.
Separate a documented next-phase decision from any claimed production deployment.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: GOV.UK discovery guidance connects problem definition, constraints and success measures to the decision about a next phase. This scoped source fact was checked on 15 October 2026. The guide's broader workflow and examples remain Atlas proposals, not demonstrated outcomes.

catalog.applicability: Use when deciding how to introduce an automation and expand it in steps, from a baseline and bounded trial through controlled use to measured expansion, with acceptance criteria agreed with the owners before results are collected.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
